sph_interpretive_translation: One who gives what is requested and authorized by the owner commits no wrongdoing.
jurisprudential_principles: Action without transgressive intent is dharmically neutral
Restoration occurs through alignment with rightful authority
Capacity to give determines lawful transfer
executable_legal_axioms: IF (consent(owner) == TRUE AND action(requested_item) == given) THEN liability = FALSE
IF (intent.transgression == FALSE AND authority.present == TRUE) THEN act.dharma_status = aligned
IF (ownership.claim == valid AND transfer.permission == explicit) THEN act.karmic_clearance = granted
supreme_court_application: In adjudication, when a party transfers property or resource under clear authorization of the lawful owner, no civil or criminal liability arises. The court must verify presence of informed consent and absence of coercion as threshold conditions for nullifying claim of wrongdoing.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that since the act was preceded by clear permission, there is no adharmic imprint. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows no deviation from svadharma of the giver. Responsibility remains with the authorizing owner. Thus, punitive response has no causal basis.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Realign parties to original intent of transaction
Restore energetic integrity of exchanged item via acknowledgment ritual
Confirm capacity of giver at time of transfer
Reintegrate actor into community trust matrix upon validation of alignment
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law flows directly from His Avataric Intelligence. Dharma is restored through recognition of rightful giving. Reality reflects non-punitive truth. Consciousness alone adjudicates.
